overview: Black develops the bishop to c5 against f2 and the usual reply is 3.Nf3 d6 or 3.Bc4 Nf6 (Italian-style transposition) with Qg4 tricks in some lines. White chooses between a quiet Italian-style development and the Vienna's f4 break. Play is open but not forcing, with White often building a centre with d3 or f4 and Black equalising with ...d6 and ...Nf6.

white_ideas.idea: Nf3 and Na4 or Bc4 to hit f7 and the c5 bishop
Delayed f4 or d3/Be3 for a flexible centre
Qg4 raids against g7 when Black's knight is on f6 or the pieces are undeveloped

black_ideas.idea: Pressure f2 with the c5 bishop, and break with ...d5
Trade off White's active pieces and equalise

typical_structures.structure: Italian-like with d3/e4 against d6/e5, Giuoco Pianissimo shape
Vienna with f4 after Nf3 d6 and f-pawn tension

character.notes: Mostly open but quiet play, with tactical tricks like Qg4 and Nxe5 if either side errs, otherwise balanced.

gambit.notes: No pawn is sacrificed in the main lines.

structure.notes: Italian-style, centre in tension with d3, so flexible.

approach.notes: A recognised, if less common, line, consistent with the Vienna being a standard if rare choice.

level.notes: Straightforward development and tricks to know, not heavy theory.

sublines_that_differ.name: 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.d3
sublines_that_differ.how: Becomes an Italian Giuoco Pianissimo with a quiet manoeuvring game.

sublines_that_differ.name: 3.Qg4
sublines_that_differ.how: Sharp tactical Qg4 lines targeting g7.

character.reason: Open development game without strong forcing play.

structure.reason: Italian-style centre in tension with d3.

approach.reason: Played by respectable players as a sideline.

level.reason: Simple plans with some move-order care.

plans.reason: White bishops and knights usually target f7.
